rationale:
Evidence from the development simulator (60 trials, 0 finishes): every run ended off track. Progress was only 0.03 to 0.12, max_error sat at about 0.061 m (the 0.06 m off-track limit), and each run recorded one line-loss event. The robot is leaving the tape early and does not recover. Steering oscillation is low (about 0.07), so the problem is not jitter. The likely cause is that the correction is too weak for the bends at this speed. kp = 1.5 gives a turn of only about 1.5 x 350 PWM per unit of signal, and the signal is a weighted average that shrinks when only the outer sensors see tape. The robot reaches the limit before it can turn back.

Changes: (1) kp 1.5 -> 3.0, roughly doubling steering authority so that a small lateral offset produces a faster correction. (2) kd 0.05 -> 0.2, adding damping so the stronger proportional term does not overshoot across the line. (3) base_speed 1.6 -> 1.3, giving the stronger steering more time to act at each bend. This costs some speed, so the 3 s finish may be marginal. I will treat completion as a secondary goal and first confirm that the robot stays on the line. (4) Geometry unchanged, so the effect of the controller change is isolated. ki stays 0 to avoid windup on curves. line_loss stays last_direction, so the robot returns toward the side it last saw.

Expected result: fewer off-track exits, max_error below 0.06 on most seeds, and progress well above the baseline 0.12. A finish is possible but not assured. Hypotheses to test: H1, the baseline failure is insufficient kp, shown by max_error falling and line_loss_events dropping to 0 or 1. H2, the speed is too high for the bend radius, shown by off-track exits concentrated on tight sections. H3, kd is too small or too large, shown by steering_oscillation. Next measurements: progress and completion_time to see whether speed or stability is limiting, max_error and line_loss_events for stability, steering_oscillation for damping, and control_effort to check that the gain is not excessive.
